title: Inert etale comparisons descend to etale quotient comparisons
statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group acting on separated [def-weil-proper-morphism] locally Noetherian schemes $U,V$ [pqf-def-locnoeth], each covered by invariant affine opens, and let $h:V\to U$ be a $G$-equivariant etale morphism [def-weil-etale-morphism]. For a geometric point $v$ [def-weil-geometric-point] put $G_v=\{g:g\circ v=v\}$. The locus on which $G_v=G_{h(v)}$ is an invariant open subset of $V$. Restrict to this locus (so $h$ is called inert). Suppose $q_U:U\to U/G$ and $q_V:V\to V/G$ are finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] surjective scheme quotients (the invariant quotient notion of [def-per-admissible-finite-scheme-quotient]) with orbit geometric fibres and invariant structure sheaves. Then $\bar h:V/G\to U/G$ is etale, and
$$V\simeq U\times_{U/G}(V/G)$$
with fibre product as in [def-pc-fibre-product], compatibly with the quotient maps and $G$-actions. These assertions hold locally on the quotients, so apply to pointed etale neighborhoods and are compatible with composition.

In addition suppose $M_U,M_V$ are fs log structures [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], $h$ is strict [def-trf-log-ideal-chart-presentation] and equivariant as a log morphism for the log actions [def-per-fs-log-group-action], both actions are very tame [def-per-very-tame-fs-log-action], and their quotient log structures are $N_U=(q_{U*}M_U)^G$ and $N_V=(q_{V*}M_V)^G$. Here strict means that the source log structure is pulled back from the target; very tame means that geometric stabilizers have invertible order and act trivially on the characteristic monoid and the strict local log stratum (the quotient of the strict local ring by the images of nonunit log sections). Then the induced log morphism [def-trf-fine-log-scheme-morphisms] $\bar h$ is strict for $N_V,N_U$.

source.place: Tag 0DT9, lemma-etale, specialized to finite constant action groupoids; log strictness is ILO VIII Proposition 5.4.2, pp.126--127; inert localization as in VIII 5.3.6--5.3.7.

proof.text: For $g\in G$ let $U^g,V^g$ be the equalizer closed subschemes of $g$ and the identity. They are closed because the schemes are separated. Equivariance gives $V^g\subset Z_g=V\times_U U^g$. On $Z_g$, the morphisms $g$ and the identity have the same composite with $h$, so this inclusion is a pullback of $\Delta_h$. The diagonal is open by [def-weil-etale-morphism] and [def-weil-unramified-morphism], and closed by separatedness (it is a pullback of the absolute diagonal of $V$). Thus $V^g$ is open and closed in $Z_g$. The bad locus $|Z_g|\setminus|V^g|$ is closed in $V$. Its finite union over $g$ is exactly the locus where some $g$ fixes $h(v)$ but not $v$. Its complement is open, and conjugation permutes these bad loci, so it is invariant. This proves the asserted inert localization, including its scheme-theoretic fixed-locus interpretation.

source.place: Tag 0DT9, lemma-etale, proof specialized to finite constant action groupoids

proof.text: Work henceforth on the inert locus. The quotient universal property gives $\bar h$ from the invariant morphism $q_Uh$. Around any point of $V/G$ take affine opens $N\subset V/G$ and $M\subset U/G$ with $\bar h(N)\subset M$. Finiteness of the quotient maps makes their inverse images affine by [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Write these inverse images as $\operatorname{Spec}B$ and $\operatorname{Spec}A$, and $M=\operatorname{Spec}C$, $N=\operatorname{Spec}D$. The invariant structure-sheaf hypotheses give $C=A^G$ and $D=B^G$. The map $A\to B$ is etale and finitely presented by [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation]. Both $A$ over $C$ and $B$ over $D$ are finite modules. All further constructions are over these quotient charts. Morphisms between affine schemes are separated, so the restricted $h$ is separated.

source.place: Tag 0DT9, lemma-etale, proof specialized to finite constant action groupoids

proof.text: For every flat $C$-algebra $E$, invariants commute with tensoring by $E$. Indeed, for either $L=A$ or $L=B$ the sequence $0\to L^G\to L\xrightarrow{\delta}\prod_{g\in G}L$ is exact, where $\delta(l)=(g(l)-l)_g$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact]. Tensoring commutes with this finite product, by the componentwise maps on pure tensors and their inverse summing the finitely many coordinate inclusions. The resulting kernel is $(E\otimes_C L)^G$, so $E\otimes_C L^G\cong(E\otimes_C L)^G$. These are algebra isomorphisms because the comparisons send $e\otimes l$ to the same tensor and preserve multiplication. In particular the base-changed quotients are $\operatorname{Spec}E$ and $\operatorname{Spec}(E\otimes_C D)$. The finite maps retain their geometric orbit fibres: on any algebraically closed field the base-change square just specifies the same common base point. No averaging or invertibility of $|G|$ is used.

source.place: Tag 03BK, lemma-invariants-base-change (3), kernel calculation; used in Tag 0DT9

proof.text: Fix a geometric point $\bar n$ of $N$ and its image $\bar m$ of $M$. Put $H=\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{M,\bar m}$. By [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit] this is the filtered colimit of coordinate rings $C_i$ of affine pointed etale neighborhoods of $\bar m$; by [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-local-structure] it is strictly henselian local. Each $C_i$ is flat over $C$. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-algebras-underlying-module] and [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-flat-modules] shows that $H$ is flat over $C$, so Step 3 applies. The pointed evaluation into the algebraically closed field of $\bar n$ has image in the relative separable closure of the residue field of $\bar m$ and is surjective onto that separable closure by [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-point-evaluation-image] and [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-point-evaluation-properties]. Its kernel is therefore maximal, hence is the maximal ideal of the local ring $H$. Thus $\bar n$ lifts to a geometric point $\bar n_H$ over the closed point of $\operatorname{Spec}H$. Write $A_H=H\otimes_C A$, $B_H=H\otimes_C B$, $D_H=H\otimes_C D$.

source.place: Tag 0DT9, lemma-etale, proof specialized to finite constant action groupoids

proof.text: The finite $H$-algebra $A_H$ is a finite product of finite henselian local $H$-algebras $A_j$ by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-henselian-local-product]. The corresponding spectra $U_j$ are clopen components by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-affine-coproduct-spectrum]. Their residue fields are finite over the separably closed residue field of $H$, and are separably closed with unique embeddings into an algebraic closure by [lem-weil-pbc-sepclosed-finite-extension-unique-embedding]. Thus each component has exactly one geometric point over the fixed closed geometric point of $H$. The orbit-fibre hypothesis makes $G$ transitive on these components. The subgroup $K$ preserving a chosen component $U_j$ is exactly the stabilizer of its closed geometric point $\bar u$: a component-preserving element induces an automorphism of its residue field over that of $H$, and uniqueness of the embedding forces this automorphism to fix the geometric point. These conclusions include nonreduced finite algebras.

source.place: Tag 0DT9, lemma-etale, proof specialized to finite constant action groupoids

proof.text: Base change preserves etaleness by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits], so $h_H$ is etale. Choose a geometric lift $\bar v$ of $\bar n_H$ to $\operatorname{Spec}B_H$, and let $\bar u=h(\bar v)$ lie on $U_j$. Such a lift exists because the finite quotient is surjective with geometric orbit fibres. Etaleness over the separably closed residue field of $A_j$ gives a rational point with the specified geometric lift, by [lem-exc-etale-lift-sepclosed-base]. Hence its residue field is exactly that of $A_j$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-henselian-etale-retraction] to the etale affine scheme over $U_j$ obtained by restricting $h_H$. It gives a unique section through this point. Its image $W_j$ is clopen and maps isomorphically to $U_j$ by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-section-clopen-immersion]. The uniqueness here is uniqueness with the specified closed point, not uniqueness of an arbitrary section of the whole etale scheme.

source.place: Tag 0DT9, lemma-etale, proof specialized to finite constant action groupoids

proof.text: For $k\in K=G_{\bar u}$, inertness gives $k\bar v=\bar v$. Conjugating the section of Step 6 by $k$ gives another section over $U_j$ with the same closed point; the uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-henselian-etale-retraction] makes it the same section. Therefore $K$ preserves $W_j$. The translates $gW_j$, indexed by $G/K$, lie over the distinct components $gU_j$, are disjoint, and together form an invariant clopen subscheme $W\subset\operatorname{Spec}B_H$. The restriction $h_H:W\to\operatorname{Spec}A_H$ is an isomorphism on every clopen component, hence an equivariant isomorphism. Moreover $W$ contains the entire orbit of $\bar v$, which is the geometric fibre over $\bar n_H$. This is the local orbit construction, rather than an application of a new quotient-comparison theorem.

source.place: Tag 0DT9, lemma-etale, proof specialized to finite constant action groupoids

proof.text: Let $e\in B_H$ be the idempotent defining $W$, with value $1$ on $W$ and $0$ on its complement. Invariance of $W$ says $g(e)=e$. Therefore $e\in B_H^G=D_H$ by Step 3. Splitting a ring by its idempotent gives $B_H=eB_H\times(1-e)B_H$, equivariantly, so $eD_H=(eB_H)^G$. Step 7 identifies $eB_H$ equivariantly with $A_H$, hence $eD_H\cong A_H^G=H$ as $H$-algebras. Consequently $\operatorname{Spec}D_H$ has a clopen neighborhood of $\bar n_H$ isomorphic to $\operatorname{Spec}H$, and over it the comparison $\operatorname{Spec}B_H\to\operatorname{Spec}A_H\times_H\operatorname{Spec}D_H$ is the isomorphism of Step 7. These are the explicit quotient and cartesian identifications of the local construction.

source.place: Tag 0DT9, lemma-etale, proof specialized to finite constant action groupoids

proof.text: Descend first the idempotent. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-algebras-tensor-elementwise] with $R=C$, stage algebras $C_i$, and module/algebra $B$. It represents $e$ by $e_i\in B_i=C_i\otimes_C B$ at some pointed etale neighborhood. The finitely many zero equations $e_i^2-e_i=0$ and $g(e_i)-e_i=0$ hold after a further common refinement, by part (2) of that node and filteredness. Thus $e_i$ is an invariant idempotent. Since $C_i$ is flat over $C$, Step 3 gives $D_i=C_i\otimes_C D=B_i^G$, so $e_i$ is also an idempotent of $D_i$. Its clopen subscheme contains the distinguished point induced by $\bar n$, since $e$ evaluates to $1$ there and all cone legs preserve that evaluation.

source.place: Tag 0DT9, lemma-etale, proof specialized to finite constant action groupoids

proof.text: Descend the isomorphism $A_H\to eB_H$ with its actual structural map. By Step 2, $B$ has a finite presentation over $A$. Hence $e_iB_i=B_i[1/e_i]$ has a finite presentation over $A_i=C_i\otimes_C A$: base-change that presentation and adjoin an inverse for $e_i$. Write it $A_i[t_1,\ldots,t_s]/(f_1,\ldots,f_r)$. The inverse over $H$ sends these generators to finitely many elements of $A_H$. Lift those elements to a later $A_{i'}$, and then force the finitely many relations $f_a$ to vanish at a further stage, using [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-algebras-tensor-elementwise] with module $A$. This gives an $A_{i'}$-algebra retraction of $A_{i'}\to e_{i'}B_{i'}$. Its other composite is the identity after tensoring with $H$; force equality on the finitely many $t_b$ at a later stage by the same node with $R=C$ and module $B$: each difference is an element of the direct summand $e_{i'}B_{i'}\subset B_{i'}$, so it suffices to kill that element in $B$ at a later stage. Thus the structural map is already an isomorphism $A_{i'}\cong e_{i'}B_{i'}$. Because it is the structural map and $e_{i'}$ is invariant, it is equivariant and so is its inverse. Step 3 now gives $C_{i'}\cong e_{i'}D_{i'}$. This supplies the finite-stage clopen quotient neighborhood with both required isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 0DT9, lemma-etale, proof specialized to finite constant action groupoids

proof.text: For every geometric point of $N$ the construction gives $T=\operatorname{Spec}C_i$, identified with the clopen $\operatorname{Spec}(e_iD_i)\subset N\times_M\operatorname{Spec}C_i$. The map $T\to N$ is etale by base change and restriction, and its image contains that point. Taking all these maps gives an etale surjection $\coprod T\to N$. Each composite $T\to N\to M$ is the original etale pointed neighborhood. Apply [lem-trf-etale-descent-through-source-cover] to conclude that $\bar h:N\to M$ is etale. Over each $T$, Step 10 identifies the canonical comparison $V\to U\times_M N$ with an isomorphism. To descend it, cover any affine open of $U\times_MN$ by the affine refinements of the pulled-back etale maps $T$; choose finitely many, since the affine open is quasi-compact. Their disjoint union is a flat surjective quasi-compact morphism onto that affine open. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-descend-isomorphism]. The local isomorphisms glue because each is inverse to the same canonical comparison. They are equivariant because that comparison is equivariant.

source.place: Tag 0DT9, lemma-etale, proof specialized to finite constant action groupoids

proof.text: For clarity about coefficients, inverse image along an etale map $j:Y\to X$ is restriction also for monoid sheaves. In the set-valued inverse-image formula of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-algebraic-structures], for an etale $T\to Y$ use the pair $(T\to X,\,T\to Y\times_XT)$ given by the graph. The adjunction of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-localization-functor-adjoint] says that any other pair receives the unique map from this pair. With the contravariant sheaf transition maps this gives the terminal value $F(T\to X)$ in the colimit. These values already form a sheaf, because a covering over $Y$ is the same covering of the underlying etale $X$-schemes. Thus no sheafification changes them. Multiplication and unit are preserved objectwise, proving the restriction formula for sheaves of commutative monoids. The etale structure sheaf restricts to $\mathcal O_Y$, since its value on $T$ is $\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$ in both sites. Its unit subsheaf therefore restricts to $\mathcal O_Y^\times$.

source.place: VIII Proposition 5.4.2, pp.126--127; elementary small-etale-site restriction argument in the etale case

proof.text:
Now assume the log hypotheses. Strictness of $h$ means $M_V\cong h^*M_U$; Step 12 identifies $h^*M_U$ with restriction $h^{-1}M_U$, since both the structure sheaf and its units restrict identically. On any etale $T\to V/G$, the scheme $U\times_{U/G}T$ is canonically $V\times_{V/G}T$ by Step 11. Hence the two monoids
$$ (\bar h^{-1}N_U)(T)=M_U(U\times_{U/G}T)^G,\qquad N_V(T)=M_V(V\times_{V/G}T)^G $$
are identified by the strict equivariant restriction of $h$. This identification commutes with all restrictions, monoid operations and structure maps. It is the quotient log morphism, because on sections it is the given pullback along $h$. Step 12 applied to the etale map $\bar h$ identifies its log pullback with inverse-image restriction, so $\bar h^*N_U\cong N_V$. This proves strictness. The fs and very-tame assumptions and the assertion that the displayed invariant sheaves are quotient log structures are retained; the etale case needs no separate chart or quotient-existence theorem.

source.place: VIII Proposition 5.4.2, pp.126--127, etale equal-group case; direct restriction computation

proof.text: All the comparisons above are the canonical maps determined by $(h,q_V)$ into the fibre product. Restriction to a quotient open, or pullback along a pointed etale neighborhood, restricts these same two components, so gives the same comparison by the fibre-product universal property. For composable inert equivariant etale maps the stabilizer equalities compose; the composite pair defining the comparison is the composite of the two component pairs. The universal property therefore identifies the composite comparison with that of the composite map. For log structures the monoid identifications of Step 13 are literal restrictions of sections; successive restrictions equal restriction along the composite. This proves both locality and the stated composition compatibility, including the pointed versions.

statement_change.old_statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group acting on separated [def-weil-proper-morphism] locally Noetherian schemes $U,V$ [pqf-def-locnoeth], each covered by invariant affine opens, and let $h:V\to U$ be a $G$-equivariant etale morphism [def-weil-etale-morphism]. For a geometric point $v$ [def-weil-geometric-point] put $G_v=\{g:g\circ v=v\}$. The locus on which $G_v=G_{h(v)}$ is an invariant open subset of $V$. Restrict to this locus (so $h$ is called inert). Suppose $q_U:U\to U/G$ and $q_V:V\to V/G$ are finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] surjective scheme quotients with orbit geometric fibres and invariant structure sheaves. Then $\bar h:V/G\to U/G$ is etale, and
$$V\simeq U\times_{U/G}(V/G)$$
with fibre product as in [def-pc-fibre-product], compatibly with the quotient maps and $G$-actions. These assertions hold locally on the quotients, so apply to pointed etale neighborhoods and are compatible with composition.

In addition suppose $M_U,M_V$ are fs log structures [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], $h$ is strict, both actions are very tame, and their quotient log structures are $N_U=(q_{U*}M_U)^G$ and $N_V=(q_{V*}M_V)^G$. Here strict means that the source log structure is pulled back from the target; very tame means that geometric stabilizers have invertible order and act trivially on the characteristic monoid and the strict local log stratum (the quotient of the strict local ring by the images of nonunit log sections). Then $\bar h$ is strict for $N_V,N_U$.
statement_change.what: The log clause specified equivariance only of the underlying scheme morphism and did not specify that the given strict log morphism is equivariant for the log actions. Without this the given pullback need not preserve invariant log sections, so the induced quotient log morphism is not defined. Explicitly require log equivariance, as ILO VIII Proposition 5.4.2 does. Added references to already landed definitions for the existing notions; the scheme assertion is unchanged.
